messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan] sample covariance and correlation functions (#1284)
parts:
Hi, just one thing.  We currently have mean() and var(), so for parallelism these should just be cov() and corr().
A

On Feb 6, 2015, at 7:36 PM, Bob Carpenter <notifi...@github.com> wrote:

It'd be nice to have sample covariance and correlation functions. 

matrix[K,K] sample_cov(matrix[N,K] x);

matrix[K,K] sample_corr(matrix[N,K] x);

Should we have the following three signatures or maybe just the first two?

matrix[K,K] sample_cov(vector[K] x[N]);  
matrix[K,K] sample_cov(row_vector[K] x[N]);  
matrix[K,K] sample_cov(real x[N,K]);

I'd suggest a simple implementation in stan/math based on Eigen::Matrix that we'd just autodiff through for var and fvar:

template <typename T>
Matrix<T,Dynamic,Dynamic> sample_cov(const Matrix<T,Dynamic,Dynamic>& x);

template <typename T>
Matrix<T,Dynamic,Dynamic> sample_cov(const std::vector<Matrix<T,Dynamic,1> >& x);

template <typename T>
Matrix<T,Dynamic,Dynamic> sample_cov(const std::vector<Matrix<T,1,Dynamic> >& x);

The last two implementations could probably be combined, but I don't see how to combine the first one with a matrix input.

It'd be a bonus if the implementation of the function could be shared with the ones using the Welford algorithm in the chains analysis.

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan] sample covariance and correlation functions (#1284)
parts:
Also, this reminds me.  We need a way in the stan call to tell it not to save certain outputs.  This comes up in the example I’m doing, because I’m having Stan simulate, in the generated quantites block, a 1000 x 12 matrix, but all I want from it is its mean and 12x12 cov matrix.  Saving something that’s of size 1200 is a big deal because it’s being saved for each iteration.
OK, sure, 1200 isn’t huge but in other contexts it could be much bigger.  It would be useful to not have to save it.  But I think that anything created in the generated quantities block is automatically saved.
For now I can do this in R so it’s not urgent, but it is an issue that comes up from time to time.
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan] sample covariance and correlation functions (#1284)
parts:
OK on the naming of cov and corr functions. But I
think you probably want a multivariate mean, too,
that takes an N x K matrix and produces the mean,
which is a K-vector. I'll update the issue.

First, you can set up RStan to save only a subset
of the parameters.

Second, if it's just generated quantities, that's
easy to do:

generated quantities {
matrix[K,K] Sigma_sim;
vector[K] mu_sim;
{
matrix[N,K] y_sim;
y_sim <- multi_normal_rng(mu,Sigma);
Sigma_sim <- cov(y_sim);
mu_sim <- mean(y_sim);
}
...

}

The variable declared in the nested block, y_sim, won't be saved.
Only the initial variables Sigma_sim and mu_sim are saved.
Same goes for transformed parameters. And nothing declared in
the model is saved.

- Bob

Yes, in R that would be called column mean, right?

And your code isn’t quite right because I’m not actually simulating the numbers from a multivariate normal. I’m simulating the numbers from a statistical model, and then calculating the cov matrix from there.

But I get your key point which is that the declaration can be done within braces. I didn’t know about that at all!

That makes life much easier. Thanks!

A
